title: feat(trigger-api): the trigger-api service serves the inbound hook from a Request, and the self-hosted route is read from http.server first (trigger-api segment 3 of ruling A on #22757)
body:
Fixes #22774
Clause-②: yes

Dispatched by the `domain:services` seat 2 PM (claim `6109841597`, branch `claude/issue-22774-inbound-hook-member`), as triage scoped the card in `6109754072`: trigger-api segment 3 of ruling A on #22757 (director record `6105447950`). Disclosure: the card is `security`, so this body names classes and positions only.

## What changes

- **The member.** `ApiTriggerPlugin` registers the `trigger-api` service and implements the optional `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook(request, hook)` declared by #22772 (`packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts`). It takes a web-standard `Request` and returns a `Response`, with no Hono context, no raw app and no `http.server`.
- **One door, two faces.** The self-hosted raw-app mount and the member both call one private body, `serveInboundHook`. It does one body read, reads one pair of header names, makes one call into `ApiTrigger.handleRequest` and answers one way. `handleRequest` holds the hook match, the per-hook secret read, the constant-time verifier (both signature forms, the 300 s window) and every status, and verification still runs before anything is enqueued. The mount hands the body its real Hono context, so it makes exactly the calls it made before (`c.req.text()`, `c.req.param` twice, `c.req.header` twice, then `c.json(body, status)`). The member hands it a `Request` adapter that answers the way Hono's `c.json` answers. The mount is not a caller of the member, and the path is mounted once. This follows the landed `webhooks` precedent (PR #22797).
- **The slot is registered wherever the trigger is installed**, in the same `kernel:ready` step that registers the `api` trigger. Without an automation service there is no trigger, so there is no slot and no mount. The boot `warn` says so.
- **`http.server` is read before the `http-server` alias.** Each name is read in its own `try`, and the first one present answers. A single server registered under both names is mounted once. With two servers under the two names, the mount goes on the `http.server` one.
- **Comment text the change made false**, kept true: `api-trigger.ts` (the `handleRequest` docblock and the class docblock name both faces) and `trigger-api-route-ledger.ts` (its header now says the server is read as `http.server` first). The ledger row is unchanged.
- **The route census learns the canonical key.** `HOST_APP_REACH` in `trigger-api-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` now matches the canonical service key `http.server` as well as the alias. `plugin.ts` reads the canonical name now, so a census that knew only the alias would miss a second module reaching the same server that way. A case for each direction is added. This is an on-the-spot extension of a guard in this package, in the same class as the card. It is declared here and in the report.
- `hono` is added as a **devDependency** (`package.json` + 3 lockfile lines). It is test-only, so the parity table reads the mount's real wire answer, as in PR #22797.
- Changeset `.changeset/22774-inbound-hook-member.md`: `@objectstack/trigger-api` minor, `Clause-②: yes`.

Zero `packages/spec` edits, no `ServiceSlotContracts` entry (#22848 remains open for it), no runtime dispatcher domain or allow-list row (#22773 remains open; whichever of the pair lands second runs the end-to-end pin), no replay-protection change.

## The PM's mechanism assumptions, measured

1. **Holds.** The member is declared on `origin/main` as `handleInboundHook?(request, hook)` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts`. Its docblock's status list is the member's spec: `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` for every unverified post, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (secret unreadable, no queue), `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `503 ENQUEUE_FAILED`, `202 { accepted, messageId }`.
2. **One sentence is stale.** One docblock bullet names only the body-only signature form ("`sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under that secret"). Since PR #22803, the raw mount also verifies the timestamped form within its 300 s window. The member answers what the mount answers, both forms included (pinned). The sentence is listed under Acceptance notes, and `packages/spec` is not edited here.
3. **Holds.** The mount delegates to the shared body with its wire answers unchanged. That is pinned by the existing 42 tests, which pass unmodified, and by the member/mount parity table below.
4. **Holds.** `plugin.ts` read only the `http-server` alias. All four registrations are pinned: canonical alone, alias alone, both on one server, and two servers.
5. **Already done by PR #22822.** `git grep -n "no oracle" d48931871 -- packages/triggers/trigger-api/src` returns 0 hits, against control `HOOKS_PATH` in `plugin.ts` (3 hits). PR #22822 restated that comment, so nothing is changed for it here.

## Evidence (head `f44f31a18`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-api exec vitest run` passes `Test Files 3 passed (3)` and `Tests 54 passed (54)`. That is 42 existing tests plus 12 new ones in `inbound-hook-member.test.ts`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-api run typecheck` is clean, and `tsc --listFiles` reaches all 7 `src/` files, the new test among them.
- **What the new pins cover.** The tests boot a real `LiteKernel` with the real plugin, plus a real Hono app for the mount.
  - The hosted shape (no HTTP server): the member answers 17 arms, each with its `code` and `status`. They cover every unverified-post class, the 503 residual, the 400s, both signature forms, the empty body, and a hand-written body verified as its own bytes. Nothing is enqueued for a refusal. It also answers the two queue faults, passes `x-idempotency-key` through, and takes the flow and hook id from `hook`, never from the URL.
  - Parity: for every arm, the member and the mount on `http.server` give equal status, headers and body bytes.
  - Composition: four server shapes, plus a run with no automation service.
- **Ablations.** Every negative pin was run with the forbidden behaviour put back. Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with the anchor hit and the write verified on disk. Each restore was proven by the blob hash equal to `HEAD`'s and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The subject resolves to `src` (relative imports, and `@objectstack/core` aliased to source), so no `dist/` rebuild applies.

| Behaviour put back | Pins that went red |
|---|---|
| main's alias-only read | 4: both parity tests, canonical alone, two servers |
| the alias read first | 1: two servers |
| the path mounted twice | 4: every mounted-once pin |
| the slot filled where no trigger is installed | 1: no automation |
| the verifier skipped | 2: the hosted-shape arm table, parity |
| path parameters re-parsed from the URL | 1: hook, not URL |
| a member header the mount does not send | 3: the arm table, both parity tests |
| a re-serialised body verified instead of the sender's bytes | 2: the arm table, parity |
| the census forgetting the canonical key | 2: both census probes |

  The first double-mount attempt was a no-op. Its replacement contained its own anchor, so the anchor count rose from 1 to 2. The tool refused the write, restored the file and ran no test. It was re-run on a different anchor, with the result above.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at this head derives 75 commands (no stale-tree warning). 74 were run, all exit 0. `check:lean-entry-closure` was re-run after building `@objectstack/objectql` and measured green. **NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`**, reason: `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`. It reads every package's `dist/` (82 absent locally), so it would need a full `pnpm build`. It is declared to CI. Reconciled with `--ran` and exit codes recorded: `75 derived, 74 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- **Lint, a proven narrowing** (the repo-wide `pnpm lint` run is CI's). `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 changed TypeScript files gives 0 errors and 0 warnings. ESLint's own JSON reports `files 5`. The population comes from `eslint.config.mjs`: its `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}` objects cover all five, and `isPathIgnored` is false for each. Invariance: the config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff cannot move any verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- **Stale spec docblock sentence** (not edited, zero-`packages/spec` scope). In `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts`, the third bullet under "What it serves" names only the `sha256=` body-only form. Today's mount, and so the member, also verifies the timestamped form within its tolerance window. The docblock's own governing line ("exactly as the plugin's self-hosted mount serves it today") stays true. No open PR is known to touch this file.
- **For the dispatcher-domain author (#22773).** If the forwarded `Request`'s body was already read, the member rejects with the platform's body-already-used `TypeError` rather than answering. That matches the contract, which says the caller answers that case as a server fault, so the caller should check before forwarding.
